_comment: Every outside service the app can use, for the Settings page: the status list, the Test buttons and the setup guide are all built from this file. `env` lists the .env names (they must exist in lib/env-settings.mjs); `test` is free (costs nothing), spend (uses one request of your quota) or none. The id is what POST /__editor/integration-test receives (lib/integration-tests.mjs).

groups.label: AI models
groups.intro: One model provider runs the suggestions, the job scoring, the CV and cover letter tailoring and the form answers. Pick one under AI provider; you only need the key of the one you pick.

groups.label: Claude account and connectors
groups.intro: These use your Claude subscription through the claude command on this computer. There is no key to paste: you sign in once and connect each service inside Claude.

groups.label: Web search services
groups.intro: Search services find postings on job sites and company websites. Each has a free allowance; add the ones you want to use.

groups.label: Free job APIs
groups.intro: Job sites that answer with their own listings. All are free. A source without a key is skipped.

groups.label: Email
groups.intro: Sending applications by email and reading replies are two separate permissions, so the reader can never send and the sender can never read.

groups.label: MCP connectors
groups.intro: An MCP server is a small program or web address that gives the app extra tools, such as a search or a remote browser. Add one below, then press Test to see the tools it offers.

groups.label: On this computer
groups.intro: Programs the app runs on your own computer. Nothing here needs an account.

items.name: Anthropic (Claude API)
items.what: Claude models, reached with a paid API key.
items.why: Reads the certificates and documents you upload to your Profile (PDFs and pictures), and can be the AI provider for scoring, tailoring and form answers.
get: Open the Anthropic Console and sign in or create an account.
Under Billing, add credits. The API is paid per use and is separate from a Claude.ai subscription.
Open Settings, then API keys, choose Create key and copy it. It is shown once.
configure: On this page open API keys, paste it into Anthropic key and press Save changes.
To use Claude for scoring and tailoring too, choose anthropic under AI provider.
items.connect: Nothing else to do. The key is kept in the .env file on your computer and read by the local server; the browser never receives it.
items.verify: Press Test on the Anthropic row. It sends one very small request and shows the model that answered.
problems: The key was refused
It was copied with a space, deleted in the Console, or belongs to another workspace. Create a new key.
Your credit balance is too low
Add credits under Billing in the Console. A Claude.ai Pro or Max plan does not include API credits.
No key, but you have a Claude subscription
Leave this empty. Uploaded documents are then read through the claude command (see Claude Code below).

items.name: OpenRouter
items.what: One key for many models from different companies, some of them free.
items.why: A low-cost AI provider for scoring jobs and tailoring documents.
get: Sign in at openrouter.ai.
Open Keys, choose Create key and copy it.
configure: Paste it into OpenRouter key under API keys and save.
Choose openrouter under AI provider. Leave Model empty for the default, or type a model id from the OpenRouter models page.
items.connect: Choosing it under AI provider is what connects it. Every AI feature then uses it.
items.verify: Press Test on the OpenRouter row.
problems: It answers 402
The model is not free and the account has no credits. Add credits or type a free model id under Model.
It answers 429
Free models have a small limit per minute and per day. Wait, or add credits.

items.name: NVIDIA NIM
items.what: Open models hosted by NVIDIA, free for development with an account.
items.why: Can be the AI provider, and it also runs the NVIDIA NIM search on the Search page, which looks through LinkedIn and other boards using the search services below so that Claude spends nothing there.
get: Sign in at build.nvidia.com.
Open your account's API keys page, choose Generate API key and copy it (it starts with nvapi-).
configure: Paste it into NVIDIA NIM key under API keys and save.
To use it for scoring and tailoring, choose nvidia under AI provider.
items.connect: The NVIDIA NIM box under Search with on the Search page switches itself on once the key is saved.
items.verify: Press Test on the NVIDIA row.
problems: It answers 404 for the model
NVIDIA retires models. Clear the Model field to use the default, or type another model id from build.nvidia.com.
The search finds little
The NIM search reads search results only and keeps a posting only when its date is known. Add Tavily, Exa or Firecrawl keys so it has more to read.

items.name: GitHub Models
items.what: Models offered through your GitHub account, with a free daily allowance.
items.why: A free AI provider for light use.
get: On GitHub open Settings, Developer settings, Personal access tokens, Fine-grained tokens.
Generate a token and give it the account permission Models: read-only.
Copy the token.
configure: Paste it into GitHub Models token under API keys and save.
Choose github under AI provider.
items.connect: Choosing it under AI provider connects it.
items.verify: Press Test on the GitHub Models row.
problems: The key was refused
The token lacks the Models permission or has expired. Create a new fine-grained token with Models: read-only.
It answers 429
The free allowance for today is used up. Try again tomorrow or choose another provider.

items.name: Google Gemini (API key)
items.what: Google's Gemini models, reached with an API key from Google AI Studio.
items.why: Can be the AI provider, and can be the reader for Check my email.
get: Open Google AI Studio and sign in.
Choose Get API key, then Create API key, and copy it.
configure: Paste it into Gemini key under API keys and save.
To use it everywhere, choose gemini under AI provider.
items.connect: For email it also needs the read-only Gmail permission (see Gmail, reading).
items.verify: Press Test on the Gemini row.
problems: You plan to use it for your email
Use a key from a paid plan. On the free tier Google may read what it receives, and the email check sends your e-mails.
It answers 429
The free tier allows few requests per minute. Wait a minute.

items.name: Gemini through Google AI Pro (agy)
items.what: Gemini through your Google AI Pro subscription, run by the agy command (the Antigravity CLI). No API key.
items.why: A reader for Check my email that needs no paid API key.
get: Install Antigravity from antigravity.google. It adds the agy command.
Open a terminal, type agy and sign in with your Google account.
configure: Optional: under AI provider, set Gemini model for agy. Empty uses the default.
items.connect: In Check my email, choose Gemini (agy) as the reader. It also needs the read-only Gmail permission (see Gmail, reading).
items.verify: Press Test on the agy row. One run takes about 25 seconds.
problems: agy was not found
Antigravity is not installed, or the terminal was opened before the installation. Restart npm run editor.
agy is not signed in
Run agy in a terminal once and sign in.

items.name: Ollama (models on your computer)
items.what: A program that runs open models on your own computer. Free, private and offline.
items.why: An AI provider with no cost and nothing sent to anyone. Slower and weaker than hosted models on most laptops.
get: Download and install Ollama.
In a terminal run: ollama pull llama3.1
configure: Choose ollama under AI provider.
Set Model to the model you pulled, if it is not llama3.1.
Only if Ollama runs on another computer: set Base URL to its address ending in /v1.
items.connect: Ollama must be running when you use an AI feature.
items.verify: Press Test on the Ollama row.
problems: The test cannot connect
Ollama is not running. Start it from the Start menu, or run ollama serve.
It answers 404
The model named under Model has not been pulled. Run ollama pull with that name.

items.name: Claude Code (the claude command)
items.what: The claude command, signed in with your Claude subscription.
items.why: It is how the app reaches the connectors of your Claude account (Indeed, Apify, Gmail), how uploaded documents are read when you have no Anthropic key, and how Claude fills application forms in a browser. It can also be the AI provider for scoring, tailoring and the ATS assessment, with no API key.
get: Install Claude Code (see its documentation for the one-line installer).
Open a terminal, type claude and sign in with your Claude account.
configure: To use Claude for scoring, tailoring and the ATS assessment, choose claude under AI provider. Leave Model empty for Sonnet, or type opus or haiku.
Optional: INTERNSHIPS_DIR in .env is the folder the connector searches run in. The default is the Internships folder on your Desktop.
items.connect: Nothing to paste. The app starts the command itself, with only the tools that one job needs and without your plugins.
items.verify: Press Test. It asks the command which connectors are connected.
problems: Claude Code is not installed
The claude command was not found. Install it, then restart npm run editor so it is on the path.
Connectors do not load
Connectors come with the Claude.ai sign-in. If you signed in to the command with an API key, run claude, type /login and choose your Claude account.

items.name: Indeed connector
items.what: Indeed's official connector for Claude.
items.why: The Search page asks Indeed for internships through it. Indeed does not allow its site to be read any other way.
get: In Claude open Settings, then Connectors.
Find Indeed and choose Connect.
configure: Nothing to configure here.
items.connect: On the Search page keep Claude ticked under Search with, and keep the Indeed tile on.
items.verify: Press Test. It reads the connector's state from the claude command.
problems: Needs authentication
Open Claude, Settings, Connectors and connect Indeed again.
Indeed says try again in N seconds
Indeed limits how fast one account may search. Wait and search again.

items.name: Apify connector
items.what: Apify's connector for Claude. Apify runs small programs (Actors) that read websites.
items.why: The Search page uses it for StepStone and Arbeitsagentur. The Actors are billed per result on your Apify account, and the rows stay in your private tracker.
get: Create an account at apify.com.
In Claude open Settings, Connectors, find Apify and connect it with that account.
configure: Optional: paste an Apify token under API keys so the Overview shows how much of your monthly usage is left. Use the same account.
items.connect: On the Search page keep Claude ticked and the StepStone and Arbeitsagentur tiles on.
items.verify: Press Test. It reads the connector's state from the claude command.
problems: Needs authentication
Connect Apify again in Claude, Settings, Connectors.
The search costs more than expected
Each result is billed. Switch the StepStone and Arbeitsagentur tiles off when you do not need them.

items.name: Gmail connector
items.what: Google's Gmail connector for Claude.
items.why: With Claude as the reader, Check my email finds replies from employers through it. The app allows it two tools only: search and read.
get: In Claude open Settings, Connectors, find Gmail and connect your Google account.
configure: Nothing to configure here.
items.connect: On the Mail page press Check my email and choose Claude as the reader.
items.verify: Press Test. It reads the connector's state from the claude command.
problems: Needs authentication
Connect Gmail again in Claude, Settings, Connectors.
It finds nothing
Only open applications in your tracker are looked for, and only mail since the last check.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.what: A web search and page-reading service.
items.why: One of the search tools the NVIDIA NIM search uses, and the service behind the remote browser that can fill a web form.
get: Sign up at firecrawl.dev.
Open API keys in the dashboard and copy the key (it starts with fc-).
configure: Paste it into Firecrawl key under API keys and save.
items.connect: Used automatically by the NVIDIA NIM search once the key is saved.
items.verify: Press Test. It asks Firecrawl for your credit balance, which costs nothing.
problems: The key was refused
Copy the key again from the dashboard.
No credits left
The free plan is a one-time allowance. The Overview shows what is left.

items.name: Tavily
items.what: A search service made for AI programs, with a free monthly allowance.
items.why: A search tool for the NVIDIA NIM search, and it looks up certificate providers when you upload a document.
get: Sign up at tavily.com.
Copy the API key from the home page of the dashboard (it starts with tvly-).
configure: Paste it into Tavily key under API keys and save.
items.connect: Used automatically once the key is saved.
items.verify: Press Test. It reads your usage, which costs nothing.
problems: The key was refused
Copy the key again.
Usage limit reached
The free allowance renews every month.

items.name: Exa
items.what: A search service that finds pages by meaning.
items.why: Finds a company's official website by its name (company discovery and the logos on the Search page), and is a search tool for the NVIDIA NIM search.
get: Sign up at exa.ai.
Open API keys in the dashboard and create a key.
configure: Paste it into Exa key under API keys and save.
items.connect: Used automatically once the key is saved.
items.verify: Press Test. Exa has no free balance check, so the test runs one search.
problems: The key was refused
Copy the key again.
Company websites are not found
A site is accepted only when its name matches the company's. A company with an unusual web address is left without one; add it by hand in the company directory.

items.name: TinyFish
items.what: A web agent service with a search tool and a remote browser.
items.why: Its search is one more tool for the NVIDIA NIM search, and its browser can fill a web form when no file needs uploading.
get: Sign in at agent.tinyfish.ai.
Create an API key in the dashboard.
configure: Paste it into TinyFish key under API keys and save.
For the search and the remote browser, also add the TinyFish MCP connector below.
items.connect: The connector is opened only when this key is saved.
items.verify: Press Test. It reads your wallet balance, which costs nothing.
problems: The key was refused
Copy the key again.
The wallet is empty
Search and fetch are free; browser runs are paid from the wallet. Add money in the TinyFish dashboard.

items.name: Apify (usage meter)
items.what: An Apify API token.
items.why: Only shows how much of your monthly Apify usage is left. The searches themselves run through the Apify connector of your Claude account.
get: In the Apify Console open Settings, then API & Integrations.
Copy your personal API token.
configure: Paste it into Apify token under API keys and save. Use the account you connected to Claude.
items.connect: The Overview card shows the balance.
items.verify: Press Test. It reads your monthly limit and usage.
problems: The key was refused
The token was reset in the Apify Console. Copy the new one.

items.name: JobSearchEngine
items.what: The separate search program in the folder next to this one (JobSearchEngine). It asks the free job APIs and feeds, and keeps to what each source permits.
items.why: It is the Free job sources box on the Search page. The app itself never opens a job site.
get: Keep the JobSearchEngine folder beside this project's folder.
Install Python 3 and the engine's requirements (see its README).
configure: Only if the engine lives elsewhere: set JOBSEARCH_ENGINE_DIR in .env to its folder.
items.connect: The Free job sources box on the Search page switches on when the engine is found.
items.verify: Press Test. It looks for the engine's folder and its Python.
problems: The JobSearchEngine is not set up
The folder or its Python was not found. Check the folder name and run the engine's install steps.

items.name: Adzuna
items.testNote: The test uses one of your 250 daily searches.
items.what: A job search site with a free API: 250 searches a day.
items.why: Real postings in Germany for the Free job sources search.
get: Sign up at developer.adzuna.com.
Create an application.
Copy its app ID and its app key.
configure: Paste both into the two Adzuna rows under API keys and save.
items.connect: The engine reads both on the next search.
items.verify: Press Test. It asks for one posting in Germany.
problems: The key was refused
The app ID and the app key are two different values; check they are in the right rows.

items.name: Jooble (Germany)
items.testNote: Not tested here: a key allows 500 requests in total, so a test would use one up.
items.what: A job search site with a free API. A key allows 500 requests, ever, and one search uses about 6.
items.why: More postings in Germany for the Free job sources search.
get: Fill in the request form on the Germany site, de.jooble.org/api/about.
The key arrives by e-mail.
configure: Paste it into Jooble key (Germany) under API keys and save.
items.connect: The engine reads it on the next search.
items.verify: Run a search with Free job sources ticked. A wrong key shows as a warning under the search.
problems: It returns US jobs or nothing
The key came from jooble.org. Each country's site gives its own key; ask on the Germany site.
It stopped working
The 500 requests are used up. Ask Jooble for a new key.

items.name: Careerjet
items.testNote: Not tested here. A wrong key shows as a warning under the search.
items.what: A job search site with a free API for publishers.
items.why: More postings in Germany for the Free job sources search.
get: Open a publisher account on the Careerjet partners page.
Copy the key from its API page.
Find your public IP address (search for what is my IP).
configure: Paste the key into Careerjet key and the address into Your IP address, then save.
items.connect: The engine reads both on the next search.
items.verify: Run a search with Free job sources ticked.
problems: It answers 403
Careerjet refuses a search without your IP address, or with an old one. Update Your IP address when your internet connection changes.

items.name: Gmail, sending
items.what: Permission for the app to send mail from your Gmail account, and nothing else.
items.why: Applications an employer wants by e-mail are sent with your tailored CV and cover letter attached, after you have read and approved each one.
get: In Google Cloud Console create a project and switch on the Gmail API.
Set up the OAuth consent screen (External, add yourself as a test user).
Under Credentials create an OAuth client ID of type Desktop app. Copy the client ID and the client secret.
configure: Paste the client ID and client secret under Email and save.
In a terminal in this folder run: npm run gmail:auth. A browser opens; allow the permission. The token is saved for you.
items.connect: On the Search page, a job whose application address is an e-mail address goes this way when the assistant applies.
items.verify: Press Test. It asks Google to accept the saved permission. No mail is sent.
problems: The permission was revoked or expired
While the Google Cloud app is in Testing, a token lasts 7 days. Run npm run gmail:auth again.
Access blocked: the app has not completed verification
Add your own address under Test users on the OAuth consent screen.

items.name: Gmail, reading
items.what: A second, read-only permission for your Gmail. It cannot send, change or delete anything.
items.why: Check my email with Gemini as the reader fetches the mail with it. With Claude as the reader it is not needed.
get: Use the same OAuth client as for sending (see Gmail, sending).
configure: In a terminal in this folder run: node scripts/gmail-auth.mjs --read and allow the permission.
items.connect: On the Mail page press Check my email and choose Gemini.
items.verify: Press Test. It asks Google to accept the saved permission. No mail is read.
problems: The permission was revoked or expired
Run node scripts/gmail-auth.mjs --read again.

items.name: SMTP (any mail provider)
items.what: The ordinary way mail programs send mail, for accounts that are not Gmail or when you prefer an app password.
items.why: Sends application e-mails when Gmail sending is not set up.
get: Find your provider's SMTP server name and port (for Gmail: smtp.gmail.com, port 587).
Create an app password. Gmail needs two-step verification switched on first.
configure: Fill in SMTP server, SMTP user and SMTP password under Email and save. Leave the port empty for 587.
items.connect: Used only when Gmail sending has no token.
items.verify: Press Test. It signs in to the mail server and signs out. No mail is sent.
problems: Invalid login
Use an app password, not your normal password.
Connection timeout
Wrong server name or port, or a network that blocks mail ports. Try port 465.

items.name: Firecrawl MCP
items.what: Firecrawl's tools as an MCP server, including a remote browser (firecrawl_interact).
items.why: The remote browser fills a web application form when there are no local files to upload.
get: Save a Firecrawl key under API keys first.
configure: Under MCP connectors press Add on the Firecrawl row. It runs npx firecrawl-mcp with your saved key.
items.connect: Switch it on in the list. The app opens it only when a job needs it.
items.verify: Press Test. It starts the server and lists its tools; firecrawl_interact should be among them.
problems: Could not connect
Node.js must be installed (npx comes with it), and the first start downloads the package, which needs the internet.
Authentication failed
The Firecrawl key is missing or wrong.

items.name: TinyFish MCP
items.what: TinyFish's search and browser agent as an MCP server.
items.why: The NVIDIA NIM search uses its search tool, and its browser agent can fill a web form.
get: Save a TinyFish key under API keys first.
configure: Under MCP connectors press Add on the TinyFish row.
items.connect: Switch it on in the list. The NVIDIA NIM search uses only its search tool, never a tool that opens a page or buys data.
items.verify: Press Test. It lists the server's tools.
problems: Could not connect
Node.js must be installed and the first start needs the internet.

items.name: Tavily MCP
items.what: Tavily's search as an MCP server.
items.why: A search tool for the site-by-site posting search (paused today because no job site permits it).
get: Save a Tavily key under API keys first.
configure: Under MCP connectors press Add on the Tavily row.
items.connect: Switch it on in the list.
items.verify: Press Test. It lists the server's tools.
problems: Could not connect
Node.js must be installed and the first start needs the internet.

items.name: Exa MCP
items.what: Exa's search as a remote MCP server at mcp.exa.ai.
items.why: A search tool for the site-by-site posting search (paused today).
get: Nothing to install: it is a web address.
configure: Under MCP connectors press Add on the Exa row.
items.connect: Switch it on in the list.
items.verify: Press Test. It lists the server's tools.
problems: Connection timed out
Check your internet connection and try again.

items.name: Playwright MCP (browser for Claude)
items.what: Microsoft's MCP server that lets an AI drive a real browser: open pages, read forms, type, upload files.
items.why: It is the browser Claude uses to fill an application form step by step. Claude never presses the final Submit; you do.
get: Install Node.js. Nothing else is needed; the server is downloaded on first use.
configure: Under MCP connectors press Add on the Playwright row, to test it here.
The Claude browser assistant starts its own copy, so this entry is optional.
items.connect: Under Applying, choose Claude in a browser as the way web forms are filled.
items.verify: Press Test. It starts the server and lists the browser tools.
problems: Could not connect
Node.js must be installed and the first start needs the internet.
The browser does not open
Run in a terminal: npx playwright install chromium

items.name: Chromium (the browser that applies)
items.what: A browser the app controls on your own computer.
items.why: It fills web application forms and uploads your tailored CV and cover letter from your disk, which a remote browser cannot do.
get: In a terminal in this folder run: npx playwright install chromium
configure: Nothing. APPLY_HEADLESS=1 in .env hides the window, which you will rarely want.
items.connect: Used for every web form whose job has tailored documents.
items.verify: Press Test. It checks that the browser is installed.
problems: The browser could not start
Run npx playwright install chromium again; an update of the app can need a newer browser.

items.name: ATS check (Python)
items.what: A small Python program (ats_check.py) that reads a PDF the way an applicant tracking system does.
items.why: The CVs & CLs page runs it on every CV before you export it. Nothing is uploaded.
get: Install Python 3.
In a terminal run: pip install pypdf
configure: Nothing. The program lives with the ATS manuals in src/assets/Student-data/ats.
items.connect: Used by Run ATS check on the CVs & CLs page.
items.verify: Press Test. It looks for Python and for the program.
problems: Python was not found
Install Python 3 and restart npm run editor.
The check reports 0 characters
The PDF is a scan. Export it from Word instead of printing and scanning.
